raw_case_text: The patient was admitted to the Department of Acquired Immune Deficiency for the first time on November 18, 2020 and was hospitalized for 3 months. Upon admission to the ward, the patient was febrile, with clinical manifestations of pneumonia - cough and shortness of breath, cachexia and candidal plaques in the oral cavity. The laboratory tests revealed severe anemia (hemoglobin values of 54 g/l) and elevated leucocytes upon admission (11,2 G/l). There were no pathological changes in the patient's biochemical profile. The patient's immune status revealed extremely severe immune deficiency as follows: Cluster of differentiation 4 (CD4) + T-cell count of 12 cells/microl; CD8 + T-cell count of 347 cells/microl. Her viral load (VL) was 10 1000 c/microl. The patient's x-ray showed bilateral pneumonia, and microbiological analysis showed Pneumocystis jirovecii and Candida albicans from sputum, as well as Candida albicans from throat secretions and faeces. Accordingly, the patient was treated with trimethoprim-cotrimoxazole, fluconazole, and antiretroviral therapy (ART) was initiated with emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide/darunavir/cobicistat. The patient was discharged from the department at the end of February, after the pneumonia had cleared, with negative microbiological tests, and controlled immune status as follows: CD4 count at 144 cells/microl; CD8 count at 1278 cells/microl. Her VL was 313 c/microl. At the end of March, she was hospitalized again because of high fever, chills, vomitting and severe lethargy. Laboratory tests showed severe anemia again - hemoglobin values of 45 g/l and thrombocytopenia - 109 G / l, with high c reactive protein (CRP) - 208 g/l, low albumin - 20.3 g/l and elevated gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) - 244 IU/l. Lung radiography showed no pathological findings. Computed tomography of the abdomen showed expressed hepatosplenomegaly. Of the microbiological tests performed, only Candida albicans was isolated from the faeces. During the hospitalization, the patient received empirical antibiotic combination - Ceftriaxone + Vancomycin, Fluconazole, multiple blood transfusions and infusion of human albumin. During the hospitalization, the patient had a temporary improvement of her condition, but a gradual progression of splenomegaly was observed. On April 20, due to acute pain in the left hypochondrium, the patient was transferred to a surgical clinic, where splenectomy was performed, with evidence of multiple splenic infarctions. Histological examination of the spleen showed histiocytic infiltration and the diagnosis of Erdheim Chester's disease was observed. After discharge from the surgical clinic, the patient was referred to the hematology department to clarify the diagnosis. During the hospitalization of the patient in the hematology ward in May, Gaucher's disease was observed, for which samples for genetic testing were sent to Germany. Meanwhile, during spontaneous bending, the patient suffered severe back pain and was immobilized from the waist down, experiencing severe back and limb pain. A magnetic resonance imaging /MRI/ revealed tumor formation and fracture of the ninth vertebra (Figures 1 and 2), similar tumor formations of the sixth thoracic and first lumbar vertebrae. In May, the patient's immune status and viral load were as follows: CD4 + T - cell count of 164 cells/microl; CD8 + T - cell count of 1634 cells/microl; and viral load (VL) was undetectable <2  c/microl. The patient was referred to a neurosurgical clinic, where a biopsy of the relevant formations in the vertebrae was performed and the fracture was filled with bone cement. The histological analysis result of the material from the vertebrae showed an infiltration of macrophages/histiocytes with abundant, mostly small vacuolated or foamy rather than fibrillary cytoplasm. Immunohistochemical study revealed CD 68 ( + ) positive abundant cell composition, S100 granular and diffuse marking; PAH8 - negative marking. Simultaneously, we received the data from the enzyme tests for Niemann's - Pick and Gaucher diseases from Germany, which were negative. Under the corticosteroid treatment, the fever subsided, but the anemic syndrome and swelling of the lower extremities persisted. A tumor formation of the skull was also observed. It was located on the right temporal bone with dimensions of about 2 cm and was painless. Following another consultation with a hematologist and after obtaining consent for performing high-risk chemotherapy, she was transferred to the haematological clinic. The patient underwent two courses of chemotherapy with Ciclophosphamid, Prednisone, Vincristin. However, she died five days after the second chemotherapy treatment.

subjective.chief_complaint: A female patient with newly diagnosed advanced HIV/AIDS initially presented in November 2020 with fever, cough, shortness of breath, cachexia, and oral thrush, and 1 month after recovering from Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia re-presented with high fever, chills, vomiting, severe lethargy, progressive hepatosplenomegaly, and pathological T9 vertebral fracture.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: First admitted on November 18, 2020, for a 3-month hospitalization with febrile bilateral Pneumocystis jirovecii and Candida albicans pneumonia, severe anemia (Hb 54 g/L), and profound HIV-induced immunodeficiency (CD4 12 cells/μL, viral load 1,010,000 copies/μL), she was successfully treated with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, fluconazole, and Biktarvy-like ART (emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide/darunavir/cobicistat) and discharged in late February 2021 with cleared pneumonia and improved immunity (CD4 144 cells/μL, VL 313 copies/μL). At the end of March 2021, she was readmitted with high fever, chills, vomiting, severe lethargy, severe anemia (Hb 45 g/L), thrombocytopenia, and progressive massive splenomegaly culminating on April 20 in acute left upper quadrant pain from splenic infarction requiring splenectomy, followed in May 2021 by acute paraplegia from a T9 vertebral pathological fracture and a 2 cm right temporal skull tumor.
subjective.past_medical_history: Advanced HIV/AIDS diagnosed in November 2020; resolved Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and oral/fecal/respiratory candidiasis (November 2020 – February 2021).
subjective.review_of_systems: Initial November 2020 admission positive for fever, cough, shortness of breath, cachexia, and oral thrush; March–May 2021 readmissions positive for high fever, chills, vomiting, lethargy, acute left hypochondriac pain, severe back and lower limb pain with paraplegia, lower extremity edema, and a painless 2 cm right temporal skull mass.

objective.physical_examination: November 2020 admission: Febrile, cachectic, dyspneic, with oral candidal plaques. March–May 2021 readmissions: Febrile, lethargic, massive progressive hepatosplenomegaly with acute left upper quadrant tenderness, acute paraplegia/immobilization below the waist, bilateral lower extremity edema, and a painless 2 cm right temporal skull mass.
objective.routine_investigations: November 2020 admission labs: Hemoglobin 54 g/L, WBC 11.2 G/L, normal biochemistry, plasma HIV viral load 1,010,000 copies/μL (falling to 313 copies/μL in February 2021 and <2 copies/μL in May 2021); chest X-ray showed bilateral pneumonia; sputum positive for Pneumocystis jirovecii and Candida albicans (throat and feces positive for C. albicans). March 2021 readmission labs: Hemoglobin 45 g/L, platelets 109 G/L, CRP 208 mg/L, serum albumin 20.3 g/L, GGT 244 IU/L; normal chest X-ray; fecal culture positive for C. albicans; negative enzymatic testing for Gaucher and Niemann-Pick diseases.
objective.advanced_workup: Serial lymphocyte subsets: CD4+ count 12 cells/μL and CD8+ 347 cells/μL in November 2020, rising on ART to CD4+ 144 cells/μL (CD8+ 1,278 cells/μL) in February 2021 and CD4+ 164 cells/μL (CD8+ 1,634 cells/μL) in May 2021. Abdominal CT and splenectomy histopathology (April 2021): Marked hepatosplenomegaly with multiple splenic infarctions; splenic histopathology demonstrated diffuse lipid-laden histiocytic infiltration diagnostic of Erdheim-Chester disease. Spine MRI and T9 vertebral biopsy/immunohistochemistry (May 2021): Tumor formations in T6, T9 (with pathological fracture), and L1 vertebrae plus a 2 cm right temporal skull lesion; vertebral biopsy showed sheets of foamy/vacuolated macrophages/histiocytes strongly positive for CD68 (+) and S100 (granular/diffuse) and negative for PAX8.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Newly diagnosed advanced HIV/AIDS (initial CD4 12 cells/μL) complicated initially by Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (confirmed on sputum microbiology) and mucocutaneous candidiasis, and subsequently (following ART-induced immune recovery to CD4 164 cells/μL) by aggressive multisystem non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis / Erdheim-Chester disease involving the spleen, liver, T6/T9/L1 vertebrae, and right temporal skull (confirmed by splenectomy and vertebral biopsy histopathology and CD68+/S100+ immunohistochemistry, with Gaucher and Niemann-Pick diseases enzymatically excluded). Plan and clinical course: Initial PJP and candidiasis were cured with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, fluconazole, and darunavir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide. Subsequent Erdheim-Chester disease was managed with splenectomy, T9 vertebroplasty, corticosteroids, and two cycles of cyclophosphamide, prednisone, and vincristine chemotherapy; however, the patient died 5 days after the second chemotherapy cycle.
